briefdescription.para: Marmot's own second-order vector-mode forward automatic differentiation: value, gradient and Hessian with respect to nDirections variables in one evaluation.

detaileddescription.para: VectorMode::Dual2nd< nDirections > carries a value, its gradient and the upper triangle of its (symmetric) Hessian. It is tailored to SecondOrder::d2f_dT2, which then evaluates the differentiated function once instead of once per pair of directions. Every operation applies the second-order chain rule: for y = f( a ), grad y = f' grad a and hess y = f' hess a + f'' grad a grad a^T, and for products the product rule. Elementary functions are evaluated once per operation, at the value.

Each number tracks which directions it depends on (a bit mask). Operations only update the Hessian rows of these directions, so the many operations on the seeded inputs themselves (e.g. the products of a determinant) cost a fraction of a full Hessian update.

It is a plain (eagerly evaluated) number type, so it may be stored in auto. Use it through the backend-neutral vocabulary of MarmotAutomaticDifferentiationTypes.h (HessianDual, seedDirection, partialDerivative, secondPartialDerivative).
